about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice B): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter Oat Protein Bites
recipes.summary: No-bake peanut butter, oat and coconut bites with chocolate chips, an easy after-school or gym-bag snack.
steps: Mix the oats, peanut butter, honey, coconut and milk in a bowl until a thick sticky dough forms.
Fold through the chocolate chips.
Roll into 16 balls with damp hands.
Place on a tray lined with baking paper and chill until firm.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 bites. Plus 30 minutes chilling.
Keep in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 7 days.

recipes.title: Dark Chocolate Topped Oat Squares
recipes.summary: Chewy no-bake oat bars bound with peanut butter and honey, topped with dark chocolate.
steps: Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Melt the butter, peanut butter and honey in a pan over low heat for 3 minutes, stirring until smooth.
Stir in the oats and cocoa until evenly coated, then press firmly into the tin.
Melt the chocolate in short bursts in the microwave, stirring, and spread over the top.
Chill until set, then cut into 12 bars.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 bar. Plus 1 hour setting.
Keep in the fridge for up to 7 days.

recipes.title: Apple and Walnut Crumble Cups
recipes.summary: Cinnamon apples under a buttery oat and walnut crumble, baked in individual cups.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional).
Toss the apple with the caster sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice and divide among six 200ml ovenproof cups.
Rub the butter into the flour, oats and brown sugar until it looks like coarse crumbs, then mix in the walnuts.
Scatter the crumble over the apples and place the cups on a tray.
Bake for 30 minutes until the top is golden and the apple is tender when pierced.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 cup.
Store covered in the fridge for up to 3 days and reheat at 160°C fan for 10 minutes.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: Rustic Apple Cinnamon Galette
recipes.summary: A free-form buttery pastry tart folded around sliced cinnamon apple.
steps: Rub the butter into the flour, sugar and salt, add the iced water to bring it to a dough, then flatten, wrap and chill.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Toss the apple with the extra sugar, cinnamon and cornflour.
Roll the pastry to a 30cm round on baking paper and pile the apple in the middle, leaving a 5cm border.
Fold the border over the fruit, brush with the milk and scatter over the almonds.
Bake for 40 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and the juices bubble. Cool for 15 minutes before cutting into 8 wedges.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 wedge. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Best eaten the day it is made; keep leftovers covered for 2 days.

recipes.title: Pear and Almond Galette
recipes.summary: Free-form shortcrust tart with thin pear slices over a sweet almond layer.
steps: Rub the cold butter into the flour, sugar and salt, add the iced water to make a dough, then flatten, wrap and chill.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Mix the ground almonds, extra sugar and soft butter into a paste.
Roll the pastry to a 30cm round on baking paper, spread the paste over the middle leaving a 5cm border, then fan the pears on top.
Fold the border over the fruit and brush with the milk.
Bake for 40 minutes until deep golden. Cool for 15 minutes and cut into 8 wedges.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 wedge. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Store covered for up to 2 days.

recipes.title: Spiced Poached Pears
recipes.summary: Tender pears poached in a light cinnamon, ginger and lemon syrup, served warm or chilled.
steps: Combine the water, sugar, cinnamon, ginger, cloves and lemon peel in a saucepan and stir over medium heat until the sugar dissolves.
Add the pears, cover with a piece of baking paper and simmer gently for 20 minutes until a knife slides in easily.
Lift the pears out and boil the syrup for 5 minutes until reduced by about a third.
Serve each pear with a spoonful of syrup.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 1 pear with syrup.
Keeps in its syrup in the fridge for up to 4 days.

recipes.title: Pear and Ginger Crumble Pots
recipes.summary: Soft pears with ginger and orange under a golden oat crumble.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional).
Toss the pear and ginger with the caster sugar and orange juice and divide among six 200ml ovenproof pots.
Rub the butter into the flour, oats and brown sugar until crumbly and scatter over the fruit.
Bake on a tray for 30 minutes until the topping is golden and the fruit bubbles.
Cool for 5 minutes before eating.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 pot.
Store covered in the fridge for up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Apricot Jam Frangipane Tartlets
recipes.summary: Shortcrust cases with a spoonful of apricot jam under golden almond cream.
steps: Rub the cold butter into the flour and sugar, add the iced water to make a dough, then wrap and chill.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional). Roll the pastry 3mm thick, cut 12 rounds and press into a 12-hole tin.
Beat the soft butter and sugar until creamy, beat in the egg, then fold in the almonds and flour.
Put 1/2 tsp apricot jam in each case, divide the almond cream over the top and scatter with the flaked almonds.
Bake for 30 minutes until the filling is golden and set. Cool in the tin for 10 minutes.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 tartlet. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keeps in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Choux Puffs with Vanilla Cream
recipes.summary: Crisp, hollow choux buns filled with softly whipped vanilla cream.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line two trays.
Bring the butter and water to a boil, tip in the flour all at once and beat for 2 minutes until it forms a smooth ball. Cool for 5 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time until the paste is glossy and drops off the spoon, then pipe or spoon 12 mounds onto the trays.
Bake for 15 minutes, then reduce to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and bake for 15 minutes until deep golden and hollow-sounding. Pierce each with a skewer and cool on a rack.
Whip the cream with the icing sugar and vanilla, split the puffs and fill just before serving.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 puffs.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg; keep filled puffs in the fridge and eat within 1 day.

recipes.title: Cheese Gougères
recipes.summary: Light savoury choux puffs flavoured with mustard and nutty cheese, best warm.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line two trays.
Bring the butter and water to a boil, tip in the flour all at once and beat for 2 minutes until it forms a smooth ball. Cool for 5 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in 60g of the cheese, the mustard and pepper.
Spoon 20 walnut-sized mounds onto the trays and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Bake for 15 minutes, then at 180°C fan (200°C conventional) for 15 minutes until puffed, deep golden and crisp.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 4 puffs.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Best warm the same day; re-crisp at 160°C fan for 5 minutes.

recipes.title: Mini Chocolate Eclairs
recipes.summary: Choux fingers filled with whipped cream and dipped in dark chocolate glaze.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line two trays.
Bring the butter and water to a boil, tip in the flour and beat for 2 minutes until smooth. Cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time until glossy.
Pipe 12 fingers about 8cm long onto the trays and bake for 15 minutes, then at 180°C fan (200°C conventional) for 15 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding. Cool on a rack.
Whip the 200ml cream with the icing sugar to soft peaks and fill the split éclairs.
Melt the chocolate with the extra cream, stir until smooth and dip the tops in the glaze. Let it set for 15 minutes.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 eclairs.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg; keep filled éclairs in the fridge and eat within 1 day.

recipes.title: Smoked Paprika Cheese Straws
recipes.summary: Crisp, buttery cheese pastry straws with a little mustard and paprika.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional) and line two trays.
Rub the butter into the flour, mustard and paprika, then mix in the cheese, egg yolk and water to a dough.
Roll out 5mm thick and cut into 30 straws about 10cm long.
Place on the trays and bake for 15 minutes until golden, turning the trays halfway.
Cool on the trays for 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 5 straws.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Store in an airtight container for up to 5 days.

recipes.title: Cinnamon Apple Turnovers
recipes.summary: Flaky puff pastry parcels around cinnamon-spiced apple.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line a tray.
Cook the apple, sugar, cinnamon, lemon juice and butter in a pan over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft but still holding shape, then cool.
Cut each pastry sheet into 4 squares, put a spoonful of apple on each and fold into triangles, pressing the edges with a fork.
Brush with the milk and cut a small slit in the top of each.
Bake for 25 minutes until puffed and deep golden. Cool for 10 minutes.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 turnover.
Best the day they are baked; reheat at 160°C fan for 5 minutes.
Food safety: Reheat leftovers until steaming hot right through.

recipes.title: No-Bake Lemon Cheesecake Jars
recipes.summary: Layers of buttery oat base and whipped lemon cream cheese filling, set in jars without gelatine.
steps: Toast the oats in a dry pan for 4 minutes until golden, then stir in the butter and honey until combined. Cool.
Beat the cream cheese, icing sugar and lemon zest until smooth.
In another bowl whip the cream to soft peaks, then fold it into the cream cheese with the lemon juice until thick.
Press the oat mix into the base of six jars, then spoon the filling over the top.
Chill until the filling is firm and set.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 jar. Plus 4 hours chilling.
Keep in the fridge and eat within 3 days.

recipes.title: Chocolate Peanut Crunch Slice
recipes.summary: Toasted oat and peanut slice set in glossy dark chocolate, no oven needed for the base.
steps: Line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Toast the oats in a dry pan for 5 minutes until golden, then mix with the peanuts.
Melt the chocolate, butter and golden syrup gently in a pan for 4 minutes, stirring until smooth.
Stir in the oats and peanuts, then press into the tin.
Chill until firm, then cut into 12 pieces.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 piece. Plus 1 hour chilling.
Keep in the fridge for up to 10 days.

recipes.title: Baked Zeppole with Ricotta Cream
recipes.summary: Oven-baked choux rings for San Giuseppe, filled with sweet lemony ricotta.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (220°C conventional) and line two trays.
Bring the butter and water to a boil, tip in the flour and beat for 2 minutes until smooth. Cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time until glossy.
Pipe 12 rings about 6cm wide onto the trays and bake for 15 minutes, then at 180°C fan (200°C conventional) for 15 minutes until deep golden and hollow-sounding. Cool on a rack.
Beat the ricotta with the caster sugar and lemon zest until smooth.
Split the rings, fill with the ricotta cream and dust with the icing sugar.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 zeppole.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg; keep filled zeppole in the fridge and eat within 1 day.

recipes.title: Spinach Pakoras Shallow-Fried
recipes.summary: Crisp chickpea-flour and spinach fritters, shallow-fried in a little oil.
steps: Mix the besan, rice flour, cumin, turmeric, chilli and salt, then stir in enough water for a thick batter.
Fold in the spinach and onion.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Drop in tablespoons of batter and fry for 3 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through, in batches.
Drain on paper towel to make 16 pakoras, then serve hot with chutney.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 4 pakoras.
Frying safety: shallow oil only, never leave the pan unattended, add batter away from you so it does not splash, and keep a lid nearby to smother a flare-up (never use water on oil).

recipes.title: Oven-Crisp Calamari Rings
recipes.summary: Golden crumbed squid rings baked on a hot tray with paprika and lemon, no deep-frying.
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C fan (230°C conventional) with a lined tray inside.
Pat the squid dry. Toss with the flour, dip in the egg, then press into the breadcrumbs mixed with the paprika and salt.
Brush the hot tray with the oil, spread the rings in a single layer and bake for 12 minutes, turning once, until golden and cooked through.
Serve straight away with lemon wedges.
notes: Snack. Per serving: about 10 rings.
Food safety: keep raw squid refrigerated until needed, cook until opaque and piping hot, wash hands, boards and tray after handling raw seafood and egg, and refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Baked Peas Kachori
recipes.summary: Flaky spiced green pea parcels baked instead of fried.
steps: Mix the flour, 2 tbsp oil and salt, add the water and knead for 5 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest.
Heat the remaining oil, fry the cumin and ginger for 1 minute, add the peas roughly mashed, spices and besan and cook for 4 minutes until dry. Add the lemon juice and cool.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Divide the dough into 8 balls and roll each into a 9cm round.
Put a spoonful of filling in each, gather the edges, pinch closed and flatten gently.
Bake on a lined tray for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
notes: Snack. Vegan. Per serving: 2 kachori. Plus 20 minutes resting the dough.
Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Coconut Lime No-Bake Bites
recipes.summary: Zesty coconut and cashew bites rolled in coconut, no cooking required.
steps: Blend the cashews and 100g of the coconut in a food processor to fine crumbs.
Add the honey, lime zest, lime juice and coconut oil and blend until the mix clumps when pressed.
Roll into 16 balls, then roll in the remaining coconut and chill until firm.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 bites. Plus 30 minutes chilling.
Keep in the fridge for up to 7 days.

recipes.title: Chickpea Chocolate Brownie Bites
recipes.summary: Fudgy mini brownie bites made with chickpeas and peanut butter, baked in a muffin tin.
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan (190°C conventional) and grease a 12-hole mini muffin tin.
Blend the chickpeas, peanut butter, honey, cocoa, eggs and baking powder until completely smooth.
Stir in half the chocolate chips and spoon into the holes.
Top with the remaining chips and bake for 20 minutes until set and a skewer comes out nearly clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 bites.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg.
Keep in the fridge for up to 4 days.

recipes.title: Apple Cinnamon Hand Pies
recipes.summary: Little shortcrust pies filled with cinnamon apple, easy to carry.
steps: Rub the butter into the flour and salt, add the iced water to make a dough, then wrap and chill.
Cook the apple, sugar, cinnamon and cornflour in a pan for 6 minutes until soft and thick, then cool.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll the pastry 3mm thick and cut 10 rounds with a 11cm cutter.
Put a spoonful of filling on each, fold over, press the edges with a fork and brush with the milk.
Bake on a lined tray for 25 minutes until golden. Cool for 10 minutes.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 pie. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Store in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Spinach and Cheese Quiche Cups
recipes.summary: Mini shortcrust cases filled with a soft egg, cheese and spinach custard.
steps: Rub the butter into the flour, add the iced water to make a dough, then wrap and chill.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional). Roll the pastry 3mm thick, cut 12 rounds and press into a 12-hole tin.
Whisk the eggs, milk and salt, then stir in the cheese, spinach and spring onion.
Pour into the cases and bake for 25 minutes until the filling is puffed, set and golden.
Cool for 5 minutes in the tin.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 2 cups. Plus 30 minutes chilling the dough.
Food safety: wash hands and the bench after handling raw egg; the filling must be fully set. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 3 days.

recipes.title: Roasted Cinnamon Apples with Yoghurt
recipes.summary: Soft cinnamon-honey apples roasted until jammy, spooned over thick yoghurt with pistachios.

items: 4 apples (about 600g), cored and cut into wedges

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan (200°C conventional).
Place the apple wedges in a baking dish with the honey, cinnamon stick and orange juice.
Roast for 25 minutes until tender and the juices turn syrupy.
Divide the yoghurt among four bowls and spoon over the apple and juices.
Scatter with the pistachios.
notes: Snack. Vegetarian. Per serving: 1 cup of apple with yoghurt.
Apples keep in the fridge for 3 days; add yoghurt when serving.
